title: Ben Affleck’s ‘Ethical AI’ Vehicle Failing To Impress Human Viewers
key_facts: Kotaku reports that Ben Affleck's Netflix film Animals, which he directs and stars in, was released this weekend.
In the film Affleck plays Mark Kimball, a mayoral candidate lagging in the polls who, with his wife Abigail (Kerry Washington), tries to raise a ransom after their son is taken hostage.
Critics cite thin characters and clunky dialogue, and online viewers have mocked some odd-looking shots; Kotaku says the film is under water on both critic and audience Rotten Tomatoes scores.
Affleck has advocated for AI in Hollywood for over a year; what he used AI for in Animals is unclear because he has been coy about it.

At a recent Bloomberg event Affleck said he does not believe there will ever be a 'just type it in' route to a movie people want to see, and that the aim was 'to do something ethical' that did not displace people.
Kotaku's own view: audiences favour work with a human touch and AI is less effective at selling tickets (opinion).
quote_evidence: What Affleck opted to use AI for in the production of Animals is unclear, as the star has been coy about the process.
The film is currently underwater on both critic and audience Rotten Tomato scores.
The whole effort behind it was to do something ethical, to do something that did not displace people
why_it_matters_hint: Affleck says AI can be used in film without replacing people, but nobody has said what AI did in this film.
event_date: Film released the weekend of 10 to 11 Oct 2026 (Kotaku: 'this weekend'; exact release date not stated).
notes: Kotaku's own reporting with a snarky tone; its headline calls the film an 'ethical AI' vehicle although the text says the AI's role is unclear. Rotten Tomatoes scores are given in words, with no figures. Affleck's quote is from a Bloomberg event, reported by Kotaku.
